record.original_question: Characterize when the norming set Γ = {γ_{g,x*} : g ∈ B_{L^∞(ν)}, x* ∈ B_{X*}} is a James boundary of L^1(ν), meaning that every f ∈ L^1(ν) attains its norm at some functional γ_{g,x*} in Γ.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.6. Characterize when Γ is a James boundary of L^1(ν).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space and $
u:\Sigma	o X$ a countably additive vector measure with values in a real Banach space $X$. Let $L^1(
u)$ be the Banach space of (classes of) real-valued functions that are integrable with respect to $
u$, equipped with the norm
$$\|f\|_{L^1(
u)}\;=\;\sup_{x^*\in B_{X^*}}\int_\Omega |f|\,d|\langle
u,x^*angle|,$$
where $|\langle
u,x^*angle|$ denotes the variation of the scalar measure $A\mapsto\langle
u(A),x^*angle$. For each $g\in B_{L^\infty(
u)}$ (where $L^\infty(
u)$ is taken with respect to a Rybakov control measure of $
u$, equivalently with respect to the family $\{|\langle
u,x^*angle|:x^*\in B_{X^*}\}$) and each $x^*\in B_{X^*}$, define the bounded linear functional $\gamma_{g,x^*}\in (L^1(
u))^*$ by
$$\gamma_{g,x^*}(f)\;=\;\Big\langle\int_\Omega f g\,d
u,\;x^*\Bigangle,\qquad f\in L^1(
u).$$
Set
$$\Gamma\;=\;\{\gamma_{g,x^*}:\;g\in B_{L^\infty(
u)},\;x^*\in B_{X^*}\}\subset B_{(L^1(
u))^*}.$$
The set $\Gamma$ is always a norming subset of the dual unit ball, i.e.\ $\|f\|_{L^1(
u)}=\sup_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\gamma(f)$ for every $f\in L^1(
u)$. Recall that a subset $B$ of the dual unit ball $B_{Y^*}$ of a Banach space $Y$ is called a James boundary of $Y$ if for every $y\in Y$ there exists $b\in B$ with $b(y)=\|y\|$.

Problem: Characterize, in terms of the vector measure $
u$ (or of the Banach space $X$ and the range of $
u$), the precise conditions under which $\Gamma$ is a James boundary of $L^1(
u)$, that is, the conditions under which every $f\in L^1(
u)$ attains its norm at some $\gamma_{g,x^*}\in\Gamma$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned related work on norming sets and integration with respect to vector measures, where it is known that Γ is always norming and w*-thick, and that Γ is a James boundary whenever the range ν(Σ) is relatively norm compact. However, no source providing a complete characterization of when Γ is a James boundary of L^1(ν) was located, so the status of the full problem appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Norming sets and integration with respect to vector measures
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Γ as a norming, w*-thick set of functionals on L^1(ν) and gives sufficient conditions (e.g., relative norm compactness of ν(Σ)) under which Γ is a James boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Partial sufficient conditions for Γ to be a James boundary are known, but no complete characterization was located.

status_evidence.title: Compactness in L^1 of a vector measure (J. Rodríguez)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys norming and James boundary properties of Γ in L^1(ν), discussing related compactness questions.
status_evidence.claim: Related questions about Γ in L^1(ν) remain a topic of ongoing research.
